intended_object: The 𝔽₂-linear isomorphism G/G² ≅ H/H² that a group isomorphism G ≅ H of commutative groups induces, i.e. the elementary-2 quotient functor applied to an isomorphism. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The forward map is `elementaryTwoQuotientMap e`, which sends the class [g] to [e g]. The inverse is the map induced by `e.symm`, so it sends [h] to [e⁻¹ h]. The two inverse laws are checked on representatives, using that the class map is surjective. This is exactly the standard isomorphism induced on G/G², and it is ZMod 2-linear as stated.

The generality is the natural one for the library's object: any commutative groups G and H, and any isomorphism between them. Mathlib's `ModN` file has no map or congr construction: it defines only `ModN`, `mkQ` and `basis`. So Mathlib has no more general counterpart that this definition duplicates. Doing the same for ModN with general n would be a different object, not this one; the library's notion is specifically G/G².
